texts.facts: Page No. 2 of 34 Brief Facts As Alleged In The Petition: 2. On 01.05.2018, at 11.00 PM, deceased Mahesh Singh was travelling by bus (accidental vehicle) from Agra to Delhi which was halted on the road near Sector 144, Greater Noida, Express Way and he alighted possibly to attend to nature's call, in the meanwhile, the Canter (offending vehicle) dashed into the rear of bus damaging the bus and seriously injuring Mahesh in the process. 3. FIR bearing No. 408/2018, PS Surajpur, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh was registered on 02.05.2018 upon statement of younger brother of deceased. After completion of investigation, Charge Sheet was filed by Investigating Officer before Ld. Concerned Court under Section 279/304A IPC. Certified copy of the same has been placed on record by the claimant. 4. It is contended that deceased was ran a Government approved retail shop for bakery, dairy products and confectionary etc earning about Rs. 25,000/- and that his untimely death has shattered the entire family. Compensation of amount to the tune of Rs. 86,50,000/- along with interest at 12% per annum has been sought for his death. Reply: 5. Notice of the claim petition was issued to respondents in Mithlesh vs Jitender Singh on 14 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134397514/ 2 response to which, Written Statements/ reply were respectively filed by respondents. In WS filed by R-1, in addition to general defences, it is stated that R-1 & 2 have falsely been implicated in this case only to extort money from the answering respondents. 6. Apart from general defences, it is stated on behalf of Insurance Company that vehicle bearing Reg. No. UP 83T 5485 MACT No.648/2018 Mithlesh & Ors. Vs. Jitender Singh & Ors. Page No. 3 of 34 was not made party in the present case. It is contended that accident resulted due to rash and negligent driving of driver of accidental vehicle. It is also stated that driver of offending vehicle did not have valid and effective driving license even though it conceded that offending vehicle was duly insured as on the date of accident. Smt. Mithlesh (wife of deceased) tendered her evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW1/A and relied upon following documents: .PW1/4- Office copy of Income Tax Return Ex.PW1/5- (colly OSR)- Photocopy of deceased's Business registration/TIN number/ certified GST. Ex.PW1/6- Photocopy of School ID of children namely Astha & Yuvraj. Ex. PW1/7- Photocopy tenth class Mark Sheet of deceased. PW-1 was then cross examined by counsel for Insurance Mithlesh vs Jitender Singh on 14 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134397514/ 3 Company. 9. PW-2 Sh. Rinku was produced as an eye witness who tendered his evidentiary affidavit as Ex.PW2/A and relied upon copy of his Aadhar Card as Ex.PW2/1. He was also cross examined by counsel for Insurance Company. 10. Petitioner Evidence was closed vide order dated 13.09.2022. 11. Subsequently, matter was listed for Respondent Evidence, however, no RE was led by any of the respondents and it was also closed vide order dated 12.09.2023.
